# TinyRustLM Full Agent Text

> Condensed full machine-readable bundle for TinyRustLM plain PHP package 1.5.0. TinyRustLM.MiRust.com is the developer portal, with the legacy runtime documentation corpus preserved under `/docs/runtime-portal/`. Deep report bodies remain in the linked durable docs rather than duplicated here.

# TinyRustLM

TinyRustLM.MiRust.com is the TinyRustLM developer portal: a plain PHP project website for a zero-dependency Rust/WebAssembly browser-local small language model runtime, custom `.slm` artifacts, deterministic validation, quantized execution, adapter sidecars, selector registries, local-only diagnostics, UAI file memory, durable reports, and project contact routing.

Current public app route:

- <https://TinyRustLM.com/>

Current developer portal route:

- <https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/developer-portal/>

## Runtime Documentation Consolidation

The former standalone runtime documentation lane is retired as a separate documentation authority. Its public implementation corpus is preserved under `/docs/runtime-portal/` with a checksum-bearing manifest at `/docs/runtime-portal/MANIFEST.md` and a current archive index at `/docs/runtime-portal/index.md`.

Use `/developer-portal/` as the current human-readable route for TinyRustLM developer evidence. Use `https://TinyRustLM.com/` as the current public app route. SLMComposer.com is no longer the canonical public app identity.

## Truth Boundary

TinyRustLM is a browser-local Rust/WebAssembly small language model runtime project. It is not a cloud assistant, hosted chatbot, WordPress theme, generic Rust site, GGUF runtime claim, or remote inference service.

Project servers do not run user model bytes. Project servers do not serve runnable user model bytes. TinyRustLM.com remains browser-local and imports local `.slm` files through the browser file picker.

Root-package public-host local import smoke maps `http://tinyrustlm.com:<port>/` to loopback for tests, treats that mapped origin as secure for browser SHA-256 APIs, imports a real fixture `.slm`, verifies SHA-256/provenance, runs Rust/WASM generation, and loads only app/runtime assets from the project host before the user-selected file. The paired `local-import-ambiguous-selection` smoke rejects duplicate `.slm` or duplicate receipt selections before local model selection. The paired `peer-url-unsafe-ui` smoke rejects unsafe Known peer URLs, including project/Hugging Face root-dot and subdomain host variants, before request/script generation. Root-package public-host share-kit smoke runs `share-metadata-kit-exec` against the same mapped root and proves the packaged root can save and execute the exact local P2P share kit, inspect peer-companion state, re-inspect it in the serve helper, start local MiniModel companion serving only after both the printed serve hint and helper inspect companion state, and validate peer-status metadata without fetching peer-piece or artifact bytes. Root-package public-host share-metadata receiver smoke runs `share-metadata-import-ui` against the same mapped root and proves the packaged root rejects chunk-list drift and wrong local `.slm` artifacts, keeps valid local share metadata at `Use Metadata`, loads/generates from the matching local `.slm`, and makes only app/runtime network requests. Root-package public-host P2P smoke runs `hf-p2p-import-kit-exec` against the same mapped root and proves catalog/manifest/feed metadata, a consenting path-prefixed MiniModel peer at `http://127.0.0.1:8123/peer-pieces/`, peer-status/preflight/preflight-inspection/import verification, receipt-chain inspection, receipt-matched `.slm` output, local browser import, and Rust/WASM generation without project-hosted model bytes; `hf-p2p-import-receipt-reject` uses the same path but tampers the receipt artifact SHA-256, companion metadata flag, final receiver-validation gate, receiver-validation contract status, and strict UTC timestamp and proves browser import fails closed.

The local browser picker can select the peer-assembled `.slm` and its `.minimodel-receipt` sidecar together. TinyRustLM validates receipt shape, strict UTC timestamp, model id, manifest/artifact SHA-256 values, artifact byte count, SLM shape/quantization/evidence fields, `import.next_gate`, peer path hints, peer base URL, companion-state URL/status, fixed chunk mode, final receiver-validation contract gates, peer-transfer evidence, companion metadata flag, and no-project-server-byte flags before showing `MiniModel P2P receipt` status and `minimodel-p2p-import-receipt` provenance. After Rust/WASM accepts the model, the Provenance panel shows the receipt hash/time, receipt sidecar, evidence status, manifest SHA-256, quantization, receiver-validation status, peer URL, companion route/status, chunk count, artifact SHA-256, and browser-load readiness summary. The picker accepts exactly one `.slm` and at most one receipt sidecar; ambiguous selections are reported instead of guessed.
Receipt-drift smoke mutates the sidecar artifact SHA-256, `peer_companion_state_metadata_fetched`, `receiver_validation.import_receipt_required_before_browser_load`, `receiver_validation_contract.status`, and `receipt.created_utc`, proving TinyRustLM reports the expected MiniModel receipt error before selecting the local model or rendering P2P receipt provenance.

## Source Options

TinyRustLM should explain model source choices as user-controlled import paths:

- Local: users choose local `.slm` files through the browser file picker.
- Hugging Face: metadata discovery may help users find source candidates, including safe `.safetensors` sibling hints for local conversion, but rows are not runnable unless MiniModel metadata names an admitted `.slm` with complete peer-offer proof and a catalog-listed or user-supplied consenting peer source. The Model Setup sidebar routes Hugging Face, P2P import, Local .slm, and Advanced tools to implemented panels rather than placeholder navigation. The simple and advanced result rows share action/source-note helpers so `P2P Import`, `Set Peer URL`, `Start Conversion`, disabled-P2P fallback, and source hints stay aligned. The simple list defaults P2P on, shows `P2P Import` only for proof-ready matches with a validated `peer_sources` row or saved Known peer URL, shows `Set Peer URL` for proof-ready matches without a known source, shows `Start Conversion` for normal supported source rows, shows `Review Conversion` for large or unknown-size source rows, warns once when P2P is disabled, and reports status buckets for P2P-ready, proof-ready-needs-peer, local-.slm-needed, external-.slm-review, and Rust-conversion-needed rows. P2P import writes that consenting direct `http://` peer into the local Rust reverify handoff; the self-locating receiver script resolves `MINIMODEL_WORKSPACE`, keeps request/manifest/status/preflight/output files beside the script, may download small MiniModel manifest metadata, then calls `minimodel check-peer-status`, `preflight-peer-import-request`, and `minimodel import-peer-request <request-json> <manifest> <output-dir>`, which validates peer-status metadata and advertised companion state when present before piece transfer and writes final receipt evidence for peer transport, piece-set SHA-256, companion-state status, fetched peer pieces, assembled-from-peer-pieces status, and no-project-server-byte flags. Catalog peer sources and catalog-declared announcement feeds are metadata, not hosted bytes; TinyRustLM verifies feed route origin, SHA-256, metadata-only feed envelope, no-project-server flags, duplicate model/peer rows, and peer-offer route/checksum/chunk-count/Merkle match before applying peer-source announcements, and valid empty feeds leave proof-ready rows at `Set Peer URL`. MiniModel `inspect-peer-source-announcement-feed <feed-json>` gives maintainers and receivers the same local Rust preflight for existing feed files. Start Conversion saves both a `minimodel.huggingface_conversion_request.v0` JSON file and self-contained local conversion script while reporting `Rust conversion script saved`; the script embeds the request JSON so it can recreate the sidecar if missing, resolves workspaces/source files from environment variables, nearby paths, or a reviewed `.safetensors` file/shard directory beside the script, then runs one TinyRustLM packer command, `convert-huggingface-request <request.json> <input.safetensors-or-directory> <output-dir> [source-shape] [quantization]`, against a user-owned local source path, writes `tinyrustlm-conversion.receipt`, discovers the actual Rust-produced `.slm` and receipt paths, and that receipt now preserves MiniModel model id, share-directory, `prepare-peer-share` command variants, catalog-entry and peer-piece globs, catalog snapshot and peer-source announcement/feed commands, local peer-serving command shape, and metadata-only publication rule. The script calls `minimodel prepare-peer-share` before discovering the generated MiniModel manifest, catalog entry, and peer-piece directory. The conversion handoff also writes a `.minimodel-serve-peer-pieces.ps1` helper into the output directory so the sender can later run `serve-peer-companion` when peer-companion state exists, falling back to `serve-peer-pieces` locally after explicit consent. If a consenting peer URL is available, `minimodel add-peer-source <catalog-entry-json> <output-json> <known-peer-base-url>` writes a with-peer entry, `minimodel write-peer-source-announcement <catalog-entry-json> <announcement-json> <known-peer-base-url>` writes portable availability metadata, `minimodel write-peer-source-announcement-feed <feed-json> <announcement-json>...` writes `peer-source-announcements.v0.json`, and `minimodel write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcement-feed <models.v0.json> <feed-route> <feed-json> <catalog-entry-json>...` writes a feed-bound `models.with-announcement-feed.v0.json` snapshot; `converted-once-p2p-publish.README.txt` tells converters which metadata is safe for catalog maintainers and that `.slm` plus peer-piece directories stay local. Catalog maintainers can also use `minimodel apply-peer-source-announcements <catalog-entry-json> <output-json> <announcement-json>...` to reject drift before shared catalog publication or `minimodel write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements <models.v0.json> <catalog-entry-json>... --announcements <announcement-json>...` to batch-publish checked metadata. `minimodel write-catalog-snapshot` then produces metadata-only `models.v0.json` without downloading or hosting model bytes. Users can load that local snapshot before Hugging Face search and can apply a local peer-source announcement JSON/feed overlay when the snapshot is proof-ready but lacks a peer URL, so matching rows become P2P-ready without a default catalog fetch. Project servers still must not run, proxy, or serve user model bytes.
- Source `hf-conversion-kit-exec` now executes the exact generated `Review Conversion` script against unreconciled mismatched shard metadata and proves Rust preflight records `source_contract_status=fail` and `conversion_decision=source-contract-rejected-before-conversion` with no `.slm`, no receipt, and no MiniModel peer-share output.
- When `KnownPeerBaseUrl` is set in the generated Hugging Face conversion script, it also runs `minimodel write-peer-companion-state <manifest> <piece-dir> <state-json> <known-peer-base-url>`, `minimodel inspect-peer-companion-state <state-json> <manifest> <piece-dir>`, and `minimodel write-peer-contact-card <output-json> <known-peer-base-url> [peer-label]` after `prepare-peer-share`. The state JSON and card JSON are metadata-only handoff data, not catalog model bytes; `serve-peer-companion` honors validated path-prefixed peer base URLs, and the `hf-conversion-kit-exec` browser smoke now verifies the exact generated kit produces and inspects both JSON files with no project-server model-byte proxy claim.
- Generated conversion/share kits run `inspect-peer-source-announcement-feed` immediately after writing `peer-source-announcements.v0.json`; feed-bound catalog snapshots are created only after that Rust preflight passes. They also run `inspect-catalog-snapshot` after writing normal and feed-bound `models.v0.json` snapshots and `inspect-peer-companion-state` after writing companion handoff state. Generated share kits honor `MINIMODEL_KNOWN_PEER_BASE_URL` for reviewed local automation, and source plus mapped public-root `share-metadata-kit-exec` executes the exact browser-downloaded `.minimodel-share-kit.ps1`, verifies local artifact byte count and SHA-256 evidence plus generated MiniModel manifest, catalog snapshot, peer-source announcement/feed, feed validation PASS output, catalog validation PASS output, peer-companion state inspection PASS output, peer contact card, and serve-helper companion-state inspection, starts the local companion server only after both the printed serve hint and helper inspect companion state, and runs `check-peer-status` with no peer-piece or artifact bytes fetched.
- Generated P2P import scripts run MiniModel `inspect-peer-import-request` before `check-peer-status`, then proceed to peer-status, preflight, saved-preflight inspection, import, `inspect-import-receipt`, `inspect-peer-import-receipt` with receipt-after-preflight timestamp ordering, and local `.slm` browser import. The executed P2P smoke asserts the request-inspection PASS output before any peer network validation and both receipt-inspection PASS outputs before browser import.
- Known peer URLs must be direct `http://` peer URLs with plain DNS/IPv4 host text and safe absolute paths. TinyRustLM rejects query strings, fragments, traversal paths, whitespace/control paths, non-plain host text, canonical project/Hugging Face hosts, `www` aliases, subdomains, and trailing DNS-root-dot variants before saving the URL or writing generated handoff scripts; `peer-url-unsafe-ui` proves the source and mapped public-host behavior.
- The local `Peer-source announcement/feed JSON` picker accepts full `peer-source-announcements.v0.json` feed envelopes as well as single announcements; `hf-peer-announcement-ui` proves the feed file path validates and applies a matching peer source before `P2P Import`, and MiniModel `inspect-peer-source-announcement-feed` covers the matching Rust preflight for existing feeds.
- Peer URL, peer contact card, and P2P toggle refreshes preserve accepted Hugging Face `.safetensors` source metadata, so source-backed `Start Conversion` / `Review Conversion` fallbacks remain available after P2P import handoffs or KnownPeerBaseUrl changes.
- Source `hf-search-ui` coverage captures both Hugging Face conversion-kit branches: the normal single-file `Start Conversion` request/script/README and the large two-shard `Review Conversion` request/script/README with `source_input_mode=safetensors-shard-directory`, reviewed-directory guidance, PowerShell shard resolution, and no Hugging Face `/resolve/` byte fetch.
- Source `hf-conversion-kit-exec` coverage executes both generated conversion branches, including sharded `Review Conversion` against a reviewed deterministic shard directory with local shard hash/byte evidence, and verifies Rust `.slm` conversion, `source_file_count=2` receipt evidence, MiniModel peer-share metadata, peer-source feed/catalog/companion-state inspection, contact card, and no project-server model bytes.
- Share metadata: after a verified local `.slm`, TinyRustLM can save `minimodel.local_slm_share_metadata.v0` with a catalog-entry candidate, artifact SHA256, fixed-size chunk hashes, chunk-list SHA256, Merkle root, and live transfer flags set unavailable.
- Peer-to-peer: future transfer work must start with secure metadata, Rust `.minimodel-peer-offer` proof, checksums, consent, one-command `prepare-peer-share` sender output, late `add-peer-source` metadata publication, portable `write-peer-source-announcement` metadata, maintainer-side `apply-peer-source-announcements` drift checks, batch `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements` publication, metadata-only `write-catalog-snapshot` reuse, optional user-run MiniModel Peer Companion design, and Rust verification before any broader peer networking.

All source options must converge on local Rust validation before a model is admitted.

## Rust Responsibilities

Rust owns `.slm` parsing, tokenizer behavior, tensor validation, quantization math, KV cache state, sampling, generation, diagnostics, error codes, adapter validation, adapter application, checksum verification, and local import receipts.

JavaScript owns browser controls, local file selection, byte transfer into WASM memory, transcript rendering, and diagnostics display. JavaScript must not parse tensor payloads or make model-quality claims.

## Artifact Rules

`.slm` is the custom local model artifact. Public copy should keep the following fields visible:

- magic and schema version
- model id and artifact kind
- byte count
- tensor directory
- tokenizer metadata
- quantization fields
- artifact checksum
- tokenizer and config checksums
- bounded runtime state
- optional adapter and selector compatibility metadata

Adapters ADP1, ASP1, and ALR1 are sidecars, not replacement models. They are not applied until Rust validates shape, identity, checksums, tokenizer agreement, tensor layout, and finite payload values.

## Model Exchange Boundary

The future MiniModel/TinyRustLM exchange architecture is metadata-first:

- catalogs may publish schemas, manifests, public keys, model-card routes, license routes, eval routes, and takedown or contact routes
- manifests must be checksum-bound and signature-aware
- Hugging Face source ids can become MiniModel metadata only after review, conversion, Rust validation, runtime smoke, and admission evidence
- verified local `.slm` imports can export metadata-only share bundles plus share-kit-ready bundles with `generated-local-minimodel-share-kit-v0` protocol hints and local share/serve helper scripts, MiniModel `inspect-share-metadata` can validate those bundle shapes plus chunk-list/Merkle/no-server-byte boundaries, `share-metadata-ui` now runs that Rust validator against the actual browser downloads, source and mapped public-root `share-metadata-import-ui` prove local share metadata reimports as checksum-bound `Use Metadata` rows until generated catalog/manifest metadata exists, including chunk-list drift rejection, wrong local `.slm` rejection, matching local `.slm` generation, and no remote model/catalog requests, and converted `.slm` files can use MiniModel `prepare-peer-share`, local `.minimodel-serve-peer-pieces.ps1` helpers that re-inspect companion state with `inspect-peer-companion-state` before preferring `serve-peer-companion` when state exists, `add-peer-source`, `write-peer-source-announcement`, `write-peer-source-announcement-feed`, `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcement-feed`, `write-peer-companion-state`, `inspect-peer-companion-state`, metadata-only `write-peer-contact-card`, `apply-peer-source-announcements`, `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements`, and `write-catalog-snapshot` to carry Rust peer-offer proof, local pieces, locally loadable metadata-only catalog reuse, consenting peer-source metadata, companion/contact handoff state, and chunk/Merkle fields before broader networking exists
- users must consent before transfer or import
- third-party model entries are not endorsements
- project infrastructure must not host, run, or serve user model bytes

Peer networking remains a later phase. Rust-native QUIC/blob transfer, Rust-libp2p, BitTorrent-style chunking, Iroh, Pear/Bare/Hypercore, and Hugging Face-assisted discovery can be compared later without making a JavaScript runtime a core dependency by default.

The optional MiniModel Peer Companion is the likely later home for local peer identity, local piece stores, cache quotas, consent prompts, direct serve/fetch controls, receipts, and TinyRustLM handoff. It must be user-run local software that reuses Rust verifier contracts, not a project-hosted byte service.

## Public Claim Boundaries

- Do not infer cloud inference or remote model execution.
- Do not claim trained assistant quality unless an evaluation sidecar with passed cases exists.
- Do not claim GGUF import support unless a specific conversion path and smoke evidence are added.
- Do not describe this package as WordPress.
- Do not introduce Bootstrap, jQuery, Tailwind, React, Vue, Composer, npm, CDN dependencies, analytics, telemetry, remote inference APIs, or external model downloads by default.
- Treat model and adapter licenses as artifact-specific.

## Agent Behavior

Read visible pages, cite canonical routes, follow robots and terms, respect the no-server-model-bytes boundary, and no-op unsupported requests. When durable memory and a UI page disagree, prefer the newest checksum-bearing durable memory entry and flag the discrepancy for review.
